decision.explanation: The provided evidence from pmid-25669829 directly supports the claim. The study is a phase I trial of pazopanib and vorinostat combination therapy in advanced solid tumors. Specifically, in the subgroup of patients with metastatic colorectal cancer, those with detected hotspot TP53 mutations (TP53 R213*, TP53 G245S, and TP53 R273C) demonstrated significantly improved progression-free survival (6.5 vs 2.0 months) and overall survival (19.8 vs 7.2 months) compared to TP53-undetected cases. This confirms the predictive association of these specific somatic TP53 variants with sensitivity/response to the combination therapy in colorectal cancer.

citations.quote:
In the phase I study of pazopanib and vorinostat in 36 patients with advanced solid tumors, detection of hotspot TP53 mutation was associated with a higher rate of SD ≥6 months/PR, longer median PFS (months), and longer median OS (months) compared to patients without a hotspot TP53 mutation. 
In colorectal cancer cases, detected TP53 hotspot mutations included TP53 R213*, TP53 G245S, and TP53 R273C.

In the subgroup of patients with metastatic colorectal cancer and sarcoma treated with pazopanib and vorinostat, those with detected hotspot TP53 mutations (n = 6) had a significantly longer median PFS of 6.5 months (95% CI 3.0–9.0; p = 0.023) compared to 2.0 months (95% CI 1.8–2.2; p = 0.023) in TP53-undetected cases (n = 10), and a significantly longer median OS of 19.8 months (95% CI 8.2–31.4; p = 0.021) versus 7.2 months (95% CI 0.6–13.8; p = 0.021), respectively.
